metrics.investment_case_interpretation: 保险集团的资金和金融投资本金主要服务保险负债、偿付能力和投资主业，折后可剥离净现金按0处理；按2023-2025年归母净利润中位数428.69亿元并打6折后，市值约7.75年覆盖折后可分配现金利润，进入赚钱且便宜榜。该口径不是普通经营公司净现金套利。

profit_quality.assessment: Use parent-shareholder net profit rather than ordinary free cash flow because PICC is an insurance financial group. Investment income is part of the core insurance funds business and is retained in the profit base because the corresponding financial assets are not deducted as detachable cash.
adjustments: Base profit uses the 2023-2025 median of parent net profit: 2023 RMB22,773 million, 2024 RMB42,869 million, 2025 RMB46,646 million; median RMB42,869 million.
No separate deduction of investment income, because insurance funds investment is a core business and the principal was not counted as detachable cash.
Profit haircut set to 0.60 to reflect insurance underwriting cycle, market return dependence, minority/regulatory capital constraints and holding-company dividend upstream friction.
Capital expenditure RMB4,784 million in 2025 is small relative to earnings but ordinary operating FCF is not the controlling denominator for an insurer.
profit_quality.cashflow_support: Operating cash flow was positive in all three years: RMB70,549 million in 2023, RMB87,990 million in 2024 and RMB118,689 million in 2025.
profit_quality.haircut_reason: Mature, profitable insurer with positive operating cash flow, but cash distributability is materially constrained by insurance liabilities, solvency and investment-market dependence.
profit_quality.cash_conversion_assessment: Positive cash flow supports continuing profit, but insurer cash flow is dominated by premium, claim and investment-asset movements and is not equivalent to distributable free cash flow.
profit_quality.maintenance_capex_assessment: 2025 purchase of fixed assets, intangibles and other long-term assets was RMB4,784 million; it does not drive the main haircut.
profit_quality.working_capital_assessment: Normal working-capital formula is not applicable to insurance operations.
